update.headline: Hotter headline inflation and firmer activity pushed yields higher, but equity risk stayed narrow: technology led while financials, industrials and consumer discretionary lagged.
update.economy: Inflation re-accelerated at the headline level: CPI y/y rose to 3.71%, up 0.17pp, and CPI m/m rose to 0.40%, up 0.33pp. Core CPI was mixed, with core CPI y/y at 2.76%, down -0.03pp, but core CPI m/m at 0.29%, up 0.07pp. PCE also firmed: PCE y/y was 3.42%, up 0.06pp, PCE m/m was 0.31%, up 0.26pp, core PCE y/y was 3.01%, up 0.03pp, and core PCE m/m was 0.25%, up 0.12pp. Growth data did not point to a labor break: unemployment held at 4.10% with a 0.00pp change, payrolls y/y improved to 0.38%, up 0.15pp, and industrial production y/y improved to 1.42%, up 0.29pp. Consensus and surprise data are unavailable, so the market read is based on the directional changes: firmer inflation plus steadier activity supported higher yields and kept pressure on duration-sensitive assets.
update.asset_classes: Rates were the cleanest macro response: DGS2 rose 11.00 bp on the day and 72.00 bp over 1 month, while DGS10 rose 7.00 bp on the day and 57.00 bp over 1 month. Duration sold off accordingly, with TLT down -0.73% on the day and -5.53% over 1 month, IEF down -0.25% on the day and -3.44% over 1 month, and LQD down -0.25% on the day and -3.41% over 1 month. Equities were positive at the index level but narrow: SPY rose 0.49% and QQQ rose 0.75%, while XLK rose 0.97%; by contrast, XLF fell -0.64%, XLI fell -0.50%, and XLV fell -0.49%. This directly extends the memory theme of narrow technology leadership versus cyclical weakness. Commodities split: oil bounced, with USO up 2.53% on the day and CL_F up 2.32%, while gold stayed under pressure from higher real-rate/dollar conditions, with GLD down -0.42% on the day and -6.65% over 1 month. FX also fit the stronger-dollar stress theme versus most majors: EURUSD fell -0.28% on the day and -2.39% over 1 month, AUDUSD fell -0.92% on the day and -3.08% over 1 month, and USDCAD rose 0.30% on the day and 2.66% over 1 month; USDJPY was the exception, down -0.03% on the day and -1.52% over 1 month.
update.predictions_changed: No regime prediction changed. The growth model gate was unchanged and the inflation model gate was unchanged, so neither forecast changed; the model refit should not be presented as a new forecast. No data gaps were reported. model_note is null.

themes_touched.title: Narrow technology leadership versus cyclical weakness
themes_touched.text: Still active. QQQ rose 0.75% and XLK rose 0.97% on the day, while XLF fell -0.64%, XLI fell -0.50%, and XLY rose only 0.10%. Over 1 month, XLK is up 5.43% versus XLF down -6.68%, XLI down -3.65%, and XLY down -6.08%, so risk appetite remains concentrated in technology rather than broad cyclical participation.

themes_touched.title: Duration pressure and stronger-dollar stress
themes_touched.text: Still active. DGS2 is up 72.00 bp over 1 month and DGS10 is up 57.00 bp over 1 month, matching losses in TLT at -5.53%, IEF at -3.44%, LQD at -3.41%, and GLD at -6.65% over 1 month. FX mostly confirms dollar pressure, with EURUSD down -2.39%, AUDUSD down -3.08%, and USDCAD up 2.66% over 1 month; USDJPY down -1.52% remains the notable exception.

sector_reads.text: Energy is in a short-term pullback, not a reversal. XLE is down -0.69% over 1 week and -2.58% over 1 month, with -2.94pp relative 1-month performance, but it remains up 17.99% over 3 months and 41.10% over 12 months, with 24.14pp relative 12-month performance. The divergence between short-term weakness and long-term uptrend looks like consolidation inside leadership, helped by oil’s 1-month gain of 6.63% in CL_F.

Financials look weak rather than merely correcting. XLF is down -1.60% over 1 week, -6.68% over 1 month, and -1.69% over 3 months, with -7.04pp relative 1-month performance. The 12-month return is only 0.70% and relative 12-month performance is -16.26pp, so the long-term profile is range-bound; this is renewed downside pressure inside a weak range, not a clean pullback within leadership.

Industrials are close to trend deterioration. XLI is down -1.07% over 1 week, -3.65% over 1 month, and -7.98% over 3 months, with -4.01pp relative 1-month performance. It is still up 11.21% over 12 months, but relative 12-month performance is -5.75pp and the long-term label is uptrend, fading. This still looks more like a pullback than a confirmed reversal, but the pullback is deepening.

Health care is consolidating rather than reversing. XLV is up 0.65% over 1 week and flat at 0.00% over 1 month, with -0.36pp relative 1-month performance. The longer trend remains strong, with 6.89% over 3 months, 16.84% over 6 months, and 27.10% over 12 months, plus 10.14pp relative 12-month performance. This is short-term digestion inside an uptrend.

Technology remains the clear leader, though momentum is labeled as fading. XLK is up 0.54% over 1 week, 5.43% over 1 month, and 40.83% over 12 months, with 5.07pp relative 1-month performance and 23.87pp relative 12-month performance. The short-term and long-term trends are aligned upward; this is not a reversal, only moderation within leadership.

Consumer discretionary remains in structural weakness. XLY is down -1.26% over 1 week, -6.08% over 1 month, and -7.28% over 3 months, with -6.44pp relative 1-month performance. The 12-month return is -8.49% and relative 12-month performance is -25.45pp, so the short-term decline confirms the long-term downtrend. This is continuation, not a pullback.
